Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the EnerGen Utilities Inc. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to EnerGen Utilities Inc.'s Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and David Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1.  Strong operational performance in our generation fleet.
    2.  Continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio.
    3.  Effective cost management.
    4.  Progress on our infrastructure investments.

Let me provide some more detail on these four key aspects.

Starting with our strong operational performance in the generation fleet, I'd like to highlight our reliability metrics—specifically SAIDI and SAIFI—and our broader system performance. These metrics are the gold standards for service reliability in our sector, linking directly to customer satisfaction, NERC compliance, and enabling the clean energy shift. SAIDI measures the system average interruption duration index in customer-minutes annually, and SAIFI tracks interruptions per customer, both excluding major events like those from Winter Storm Elliott, following FERC guidelines.

The results underscore our excellence. For the full year to date through Q3 2024, our consolidated SAIDI stood at 92.4 minutes per customer, a 16% improvement from 110.1 minutes in the prior year, outperforming the national median of 118 minutes per the EIA's latest survey. This marks about an 8% compounded annual improvement since 2020, landing us in the top quartile of investor-owned utilities alongside peers like Duke Energy and Southern Company. For SAIFI, we hit 0.92 interruptions per customer, down 21% from 1.17 last year, surpassing our internal target of 1.00 and the S&P Global Northeast and Mid-Atlantic IOU average of 1.05.

Regionally, across our Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Southeast footprints, results aligned with weather and load variations. In the Northeast, serving 2.8 million customers in NYISO and PJM, SAIDI was 78 minutes versus 95 last year, despite three derecho events, with SAIFI at 0.81 thanks to post-Ida storm hardening. Mid-Atlantic operations in Virginia and Maryland posted SAIDI at 101 minutes, slightly up from 98 due to Hurricane Lee's impacts, but SAIFI improved to 0.98 from 1.22—our strongest yet—from targeted investments. Southeast markets recorded 112 minutes SAIDI amid peak loads of 18 GW from heat waves, yet SAIFI fell 18% to 1.05, ahead of Florida Power & Light peers.

By voltage class, distribution under 69 kV led with 88 minutes SAIDI and 0.89 SAIFI, boosted by $450 million in 2024 grid modernization capex so far. Transmission above 69 kV remained solid at 15 minutes SAIDI and 0.12 SAIFI, in the 95th percentile per NERC's TADS.

Key drivers include our multi-faceted strategy. Our Advanced Distribution Management System from GE Grid Solutions, covering 85% of feeders, enabled FLISR to prevent over 1.2 million customer-minutes of outages, cutting SAIDI by 15 minutes. AI predictive analytics from AutoGrid forecast 92% of vegetation faults, up from 75%, while drone and LiDAR scanned 12,000 miles of right-of-way, reducing tree-contact outages 28% against ESRI benchmarks.

Hardware advances feature SF6-free switchgear from ABB's EconiQ, targeting 40% penetration by end-2024 ahead of EPA and CARB rules, enhancing reliability and cutting O&M 12%. Renewable integration at 25% generation from solar-plus-storage like our 500 MW Empire Solar farm stressed feeders, but 1,200 IEEE 1547-compliant DERMS controls curtailed during 99% of high-RAM events.

These metrics drive ROE upside—in New York, beating SAIDI unlocked a $22 million rider; Pennsylvania added 50 bps for SAIFI. J.D. Power satisfaction rose to #3 in the East, cutting churn 15% and lifting ARPU. For 2025, $1.2 billion capex—20% higher—targets resilience: 5,000 miles hardened to Category 4, EV substation upgrades for 30% load growth, and 50 microgrid pilots. Extreme weather risks are modeled to cap SAIDI at 110 minutes in a 1-in-50-year event. This reliability moat supports 7-9% EPS growth amid DER rise and electrification.

Next, on continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, which ties into our revenue breakdown by regulated and unregulated segments, this highlights the resilience of our diversified model. Our regulated transmission and distribution utilities in PJM, MISO, ERCOT, and SPP provide stability, while unregulated merchant generation, renewables, and retail offer growth.

For Q3 2024 ended September 30, total revenues reached $2.92 billion, up 9.5% from $2.67 billion in Q3 2023. Regulated revenues were 68%, or $1.99 billion; unregulated 32%, or $930 million. Trailing twelve months, regulated at $7.58 billion (69%), unregulated $3.38 billion (31%).

Regulated segment delivered $1.99 billion, up 6.8% YoY, via rate cases, capex recovery at 9.8-10.2% ROE, and AFUDC on our $4.5 billion 2024 capex. Transmission: $1.15 billion (58%), up 8.2%, from FERC formula updates recovering $190 million incentives on projects like the 345kV Apex-to-Gridline in Pennsylvania, plus 15% PJM MAAC load growth from data centers yielding ancillary revenues. Distribution: $840 million (42%), up 5.1%, with 5% weather-normalized sales growth from 92% AMI across 2.8 million customers; Texas heat added $48 million via decoupling.

Regulated growth projects 6-7% CAGR to 2026 from $13 billion five-year capex on hardening per FERC Order 881 and EV corridors. Three rate cases this year—two approved in Ohio and Virginia with 50 bps ROE bumps—add $470 million annually by 2025. EBITDA margins at 28%, low commodity risk.

Unregulated: $930 million, up 14.7% YoY. Merchant generation: $535 million (57%), up 19%, with PJM spark spreads at $29/MWh versus $22, gas heat rates at 7,200 Btu/kWh. Our 1.2 GW batteries, including 300 MW/600 MWh ERCOT Ironwood, earned $125 million in regulation and arbitrage at 92% efficiency; PJM BRA capacity $68 million at $275/MW-day. Renewables and PPAs: $285 million (31%), up 13%, with IRA ITC/PTC on 1.5 GW solar like Desert Bloom unlocking $95 million; 70% PPAs at $45-55/MWh with Google and Microsoft hedge ERCOT negatives. Retail and trading: $110 million (12%), steady at 4.5% margins via Texas and Illinois expansions.

ERCOT shone with $330 million (35% unregulated) from $9,500/MWh peaks; MISO wind hedged 85% at $30-45/MWh. Post-Uri, regulated rate base grew from $18 billion to $23 billion, renewables to 25% by 2027 via DERMS, synchrophasors with Siemens and GE Vernova, Southeast T&D M&A at 8-10% ROE, 45% carbon-free YTD for PJM carbon pilots. Q4 guide: regulated $2.00-2.05 billion, unregulated $950-1.00 billion; full-year unregulated EPS +$0.48/share. Risks: reg lag, gas volatility (75% hedged 2025 at $3.25/MMBtu).

Moving to effective cost management, our operations and maintenance—or O&M—expense initiatives delivered key efficiency gains, a pillar of margin resilience amid volatility. O&M is 25-30% of costs, with natgas up 15% YoY from Ukraine and supply issues, plus heat rates on our combined-cycle fleet. Yet, Q3 consolidated O&M was $285 million, down 7.2% or $22 million YoY, despite 4% capacity growth from 450 MW Desert Peak solar-storage in ERCOT. TTM O&M per MWh fell 9.5% to $12.45 from $13.78, beating S&P peers' 6.8% and matching NextEra via tech.

Four pillars: predictive analytics/digital twins, outage optimization, supply chain localization, workforce productivity. Digitally, GE Vernova Predix AI on SCADA for 85% of 12 GW thermal cut unplanned outages 28% YoY to 1.5% availability loss, saving $18 million; a day on 800 MW Frame 7FA costs $1.2 million at $45/MWh PJM LMP. Renewables: 15,000 Siemens Gamesa IoT sensors lifted SPP wind capacity factors 12% to 43.2%, saving $9 million Q3, plus $5.2 million ERCOT penalties avoided in July heat.

Outages: 22% shorter plans on nuclear/coal via modular work; Prairie Wind MISO nuclear uprate finished steam generators in 45 days vs. 65, adding $14 million at 92% capacity. Coal: idled Northeast PJM units, shifted $7 million O&M to H-class hydrogen-ready repowers for net-zero 2045.

Supply chain: 65% U.S. localization in Ohio/Texas with Elliott Group cut lead times to 16 weeks, saving $11 million vs. Baltic spikes, like Dominion post-COVID. Workforce: Oracle HCM upskilling boosted productivity 15%, overtime to 8%; 40% cross-trained on drones saved $4.2 million Midwest hydro.

Regionally: PJM 10.1% cut (FERC 2222 DER offset $3 million patrols); ERCOT 11.4% (batteries trim ancillaries); CAISO flat vs. wildfire passthroughs. $1.2 billion three-year roadmap targets 8-10% more cuts by 2025 via digital twins/AI, unlocking 200 bps EBITDA expansion to fund $4.5 billion capex, 1.2 GW offshore wind, NuScale SMRs, sustaining 5.8% dividend.

Finally, progress on infrastructure investments centers on our rate base growth outlook and assumptions. Our rate base at $28.7 billion as of September 30 underpins 9.75% average ROE across Midwest/Northeast in MISO, PJM, SPP post-Illinois settlement.

We reaffirm 6.5% CAGR 2024-2027, from $29.5 billion YE2024 to $37.4 billion YE2027; to 2030, 5.8% to $46 billion, top-quartile like Duke/Dominion.

Capex drives it: $2.4 billion regulated 2024 (up 9%), $13 billion five-year 2024-2028. 45% T&D modernization—$470 million GridResilient Midwest reconductoring 1,200 miles 345 kV HTLS ACCC like ITC, 90% AFUDC, CWIP in Ohio/Indiana adding $260 million YTD. Generation 35%: 1.2 GW renewables by 2027—600 MW Illinois solar (Rock Falls PPA Meta), 400 MW Iowa wind repowers to 42% factors Vestas-style, 200 MW BESS; IRA 30-45% ITC/PTC, 10%+ IRRs, transfer to Google. 20% customer: 500k more AMI 2025, 10k EV chargers with Electrify America, microgrids. Load up 2.2% YTD, 15% Ohio data centers (AWS 500 MW), PJM 1.8% to 2030.

Growth capex 65/35 split yields 8.2% velocity; $1.2 billion CWIP from cases, including $830 million Ohio loop-in to Grain Belt HVDC.

Midwest (60% rate base): 7.3% CAGR—MISO Tranche 3 $620 million 765 kV, Illinois CEJA 90% solar. Indiana post-May case (9.5% ROE, $190 million rev) accelerates 1 GW. Northeast (40%): 5.6% CAGR—PJM RTEP $360 million dynamic ratings; NY REV delays storage to 2026, PA wildfire 25 bps; formula rates 75% recovery in 12 months.

Assumptions: regulatory 50-100 bps ROE in formulas, 9.5-10.25% blended (25 bps slip -40 bps CAGR); 95% capex in-service, 90% OTIF Quanta/Burns; inflation 2.5%, rates 4.5% Treasury (7.8% WACC, +100 bps -15% AFUDC); load 1.8% annual to 2.6% post-2027 EVs 20%; IRA/state RPS/FERC 1920 ($2-3B opps); risks offset by 60/40 cap/equity, DOE loans/green bonds.

This executable growth delivers 8-10% EPS CAGR to net-zero 2045.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss the financials.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.48 and revenue of $2.92 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $720 million, primarily focused on renewable integrations and grid modernization. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you, Lisa. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for rate base growth over the next few years?

Mark Reynolds: Certainly, John. As I detailed earlier, we're targeting a 6.5% CAGR through 2027, driven by our robust $13 billion five-year capex plan, with heavy emphasis on renewables like 1.2 GW additions and grid resiliency projects. Key assumptions include timely regulatory recovery at blended ROEs around 9.75% and load growth from data centers and electrification. We've already secured CWIP in multiple jurisdictions, which accelerates accretion, and our stress tests show resilience even if ROEs slip modestly. This positions us for sustained EPS growth while advancing clean energy goals.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez: What is your outlook for O&M expenses going into 2025?

Lisa Chen: Great question, Emily. Building on Mark's comments, our O&M optimization roadmap is set to deliver another 8-10% reduction by 2025, on top of the 9.5% TTM improvement to $12.45 per MWh. This comes from scaling digital twins, AI heat rate optimization on gas assets, and full renewable adoption, potentially adding 200 basis points to EBITDA margins. We're funding this alongside $4.5 billion capex without compromising our dividend. Regional dynamics like PJM's aging infra and ERCOT volatility are addressed through localized supply chains and workforce upskilling, keeping us ahead of peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: How are you mitigating risks related to reliability metrics amid increasing extreme weather?

David Patel: Thanks, Mike. Reliability is core to our operations, and we're proactively tackling weather risks with $1.2 billion in 2025 capex for hardening 5,000 miles of line to Category 4 standards and deploying microgrids at 50 critical sites. Our ADMS and AI analytics already avoided 1.2 million customer-minutes this year, and SF6-free gear plus DERMS handle renewable intermittency. Scenario modeling limits SAIDI to 110 minutes in severe events, while pilots under FERC Order 2222 integrate DERs seamlessly. This has earned us regulatory rewards and top J.D. Power rankings, ensuring we outperform in any climate.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mark Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning EnerGen Utilities Inc. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in EnerGen Utilities Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
